The file is in the application layer because it matches the **/dto/** and **/*.dto.ts patterns. It declares one class, CheckStockQueryDto, which is a plain data-transfer shape with a single optional `quantity` field. All of its responsibilities fit an application DTO: it describes the input contract and validates it (@IsOptional, @IsInt, @Min(1)). The file has no business rules, no persistence, no repository or ORM code, and no controller or routing logic.

Some of the decorators are HTTP-facing. @ApiPropertyOptional is Swagger documentation, and @Type(() => Number) coerces query-string values. The folder name 'primary-adapters' also suggests the file is meant for the transport edge. These are only declarative metadata on a data contract, not behaviour, and putting such decorators on DTOs is the normal NestJS convention. So I don't count them as a misplaced responsibility under this rubric. This is a borderline case, which is why confidence is moderate rather than high.
